newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb on Sharif win.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb on Sharif win.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.07 rupees up at 41.70 to the dollar on Tuesday in kerb trade in dull activity. There was little dollar demand after Nawaz Sharif's landslide election victory, dealers said.
"Sharif's election win and a sharp rise in the stock market strengthened the rupee," one dealer said. "But the dollar is expected to gain again after (next week's) Eid holidays."
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, set on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar. The premium on forex bearer certificates was 4.20 percent, from 4.35 in the morning.
